description: Imagine sinking your teeth into a light, airy Focaccia Genovese, its golden crust glistening with fragrant olive oil and studded with aromatic rosemary. This traditional Ligurian flatbread is a symphony of simple, high-quality ingredients, creating a remarkably soft interior and a delightful chew. It's the perfect accompaniment to any meal or a wonderful snack on its own.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until the yeast is foamy, indicating it's active. This is crucial for a good rise.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons of olive oil and continue mixing until it's mostly incorporated. The dough will be sticky.

instructions.title: First Rise (Bulk Fermentation)
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly oiled bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size. This slow rise develops flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare for Second Rise
instructions.text: Gently transfer the risen dough to a lightly oiled 20x30 cm baking pan. Using your fingertips, gently stretch and dimple the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. Drizzle generously with 2 more tablespoons of olive oil.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Toppings
instructions.text: Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap and let it rise again for 30-45 minutes in a warm place, or until visibly puffy. Preheat your oven to 220C (425F) during the last 15 minutes of the rise. After the rise, press your fingers deep into the dough to create those signature focaccia dimples. Sprinkle with chopped fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Bake the focaccia in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. The crust should be crispy and the interior soft. Keep an eye on it to prevent over-baking.

instructions.title: Finishing Touch
instructions.text: Once out of the oven, immediately drizzle the hot focaccia with the remaining extra virgin olive oil. This enhances its flavor and keeps the crust tender. Let it cool for a few minutes before slicing and serving. Buon appetito!

tips: Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil; it's a key flavor component in authentic Focaccia Genovese. Don't skimp!
Handle the dough gently after the first rise to maintain its airy structure. Overworking it will result in a tougher focaccia.
For an extra crispy bottom, consider baking the focaccia on a preheated pizza stone or baking steel.
article:
Unleash the aroma of a bustling Italian bakery right in your own kitchen. Few breads capture the essence of Mediterranean simplicity and profound flavor quite like Focaccia. But among the many delightful variations, one stands out as a true benchmark of culinary excellence: Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil. This isn't just any flatbread; it's a testament to the power of quality ingredients and time-honored techniques, resulting in a gloriously airy, olive oil-rich, and herb-infused masterpiece that’s surprisingly accessible for home bakers.

Imagine a golden-crusted bread, dimpled deeply to hold pools of fragrant extra virgin olive oil, studded with aromatic rosemary needles, and boasting an interior so light and tender it practically melts in your mouth. That’s the magic of Focaccia Genovese. Originating from Genoa, the capital of Liguria, this iconic Italian bread is a staple in the region, often enjoyed for breakfast, as a snack, or alongside various meals. Its distinctive character comes from a high hydration dough, a generous amount of premium olive oil, and the characteristic dimpling that creates a unique texture and maximizes flavor delivery.

This article will guide you through the journey of creating your own authentic Focaccia Genovese, complete with essential ingredients, step-by-step instructions, and expert tips to ensure your baking success. Prepare to transform your kitchen into a Ligurian haven and delight your senses with this unforgettable Italian classic.

## What is Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil?
Focaccia Genovese is not just any focaccia; it's a specific style originating from Genoa, Italy. Unlike some thicker, more doughy focaccias found elsewhere, the Genovese version is traditionally thinner, often boasting a wonderfully crisp bottom crust and an incredibly airy, open crumb. Its signature features include a generous application of high-quality extra virgin olive oil, both in the dough and drizzled over the top before baking, and deep dimples created by pressing fingertips into the risen dough. These dimples serve a crucial purpose: they act as little reservoirs for the olive oil, which then permeates the bread during baking, contributing to its rich flavor and characteristic moistness.

The "Rosemary Olive Oil" part of its name highlights its classic flavoring. Fresh rosemary, with its piney, slightly peppery notes, is the perfect aromatic complement to the fruity bitterness of good olive oil. The combination creates an irresistible scent and taste that defines this beloved bread. It's a simple bread, relying on the quality of its core ingredients – flour, water, yeast, salt, olive oil, and rosemary – to achieve profound deliciousness. The goal is a delicate balance: a golden exterior, a soft interior, and an unmistakable aroma that hints at its Mediterranean origins.

## Ingredients You Need
Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese requires a few key ingredients, each playing a vital role in the final texture and flavor. Opting for high-quality components, especially the olive oil, will elevate your results significantly.

*   **Strong Bread Flour (500g):** High protein content is essential for developing the gluten structure needed for focaccia’s characteristic airy crumb and chew.
*   **Warm Water (400-420ml):** Around 38-43°C (100-110°F) is ideal for activating yeast. The high hydration is key for a light, open texture.
*   **Active Dry Yeast (7g or 2 ¼ teaspoons):** The leavening agent that gives the focaccia its rise.
*   **Fine Sea Salt (10g or 1 ¾ teaspoons):** Essential for flavor and controlling yeast activity.
*   **Sugar (5g or 1 teaspoon, optional):** A small amount helps kickstart the yeast, though it’s not strictly necessary.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil (100ml + more for drizzling):** This is non-negotiable. Use a good quality, fruity extra virgin olive oil. About 50ml will go into the dough, and the rest for greasing the pan and liberally drizzling on top.
*   **Fresh Rosemary (2-3 sprigs):** Roughly chopped, or small whole needles if you prefer.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt (for sprinkling):** A finishing touch that adds bursts of salty flavor and texture to the crust.

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Mastering the perfect Focaccia Genovese involves patience and gentle handling, but the process itself is straightforward.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water and sugar (if using). Sprinkle the active dry yeast over the top and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is alive and active.
2.  **Combine Dry Ingredients:** In a separate bowl, whisk together the bread flour and fine sea salt.
3.  **Mix the Dough:** Pour the yeast mixture into the flour mixture. Add 50ml of the extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a sturdy spoon or your hands until a shaggy, wet dough forms. It will be very sticky – resist the urge to add more flour!
4.  **First Rise (Bulk Fermentation):** Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has at least doubled in size. During this time, you can perform one or two "stretch and fold" sessions every 30-45 minutes. To do this, lightly oil your hands, gently pull a section of the dough up, stretch it, and fold it over itself. Rotate the bowl and repeat 3-4 times. This builds gluten without intensive kneading.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally coat a 9x13 inch (or similar size) baking sheet with at least 30-40ml of extra virgin olive oil. Ensure the entire bottom and sides are well oiled.
6.  **Transfer and Dimple:** Gently pour or scrape the risen dough into the prepared baking pan. It will be loose and sticky. With oiled fingertips, gently stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. Once lightly stretched, use your fingertips to create deep dimples across the entire surface of the dough, making sure not to press all the way through to the bottom of the pan.
7.  **Second Rise (Proofing):** Drizzle another 10-20ml of olive oil over the dimpled dough. Sprinkle with fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F) during the last 15 minutes of this rise.
8.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-30 minutes, or until the Focaccia Genovese is golden brown on top and deeply golden on the bottom. If the top is browning too quickly, you can loosely tent it with foil.
9.  **Cool:** Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly. Serve warm or at room temperature.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
Achieving the authentic texture of Focaccia Genovese requires attention to a few key details that can make all the difference.

*   **Quality Olive Oil is Paramount:** This cannot be stressed enough. Since olive oil is such a dominant flavor, investing in a good quality extra virgin olive oil will profoundly impact the taste of your focaccia.
*   **Don't Fear the Stickiness:** High hydration is the secret to a light, airy crumb. The dough will be very sticky, especially during the initial mixing and stretching. Resist the urge to add more flour; simply oil your hands generously when handling the dough.
*   **Gentle Handling:** After the first rise, handle the dough as little and as gently as possible. You want to preserve all those precious air bubbles the yeast has created.
*   **Deep Dimpling:** Don't be shy with the dimples! Press your fingertips deep into the dough to create those signature wells that hold the olive oil and contribute to the focaccia's unique texture. Just be careful not to poke holes all the way through.
*   **Generous Olive Oil Application:** Be liberal with the olive oil, especially in the pan and on top before baking. It creates a crispy crust and infuses the bread with flavor and moisture.
*   **High Heat Baking:** A hot oven is crucial for a quick rise and a beautifully golden, crisp crust. Ensure your oven is fully preheated.
*   **Patience with Rising:** Don't rush the rising times. These periods allow the yeast to work its magic, developing flavor and an open crumb structure. A warm, draft-free environment is ideal.

## Serving Suggestions
Whether you're enjoying Focaccia Genovese as a snack or a meal component, its versatility shines.

*   **Appetizer:** Serve warm with a side of balsamic glaze, a bowl of seasoned olive oil for dipping, or a vibrant tapenade.
*   **With Meals:** It’s a perfect accompaniment to hearty soups, fresh salads, or any Italian pasta dish. Its absorbent nature makes it excellent for soaking up sauces.
*   **Charcuterie Boards:** A fantastic addition to a cheese and cured meat platter, offering a textural contrast and a flavorful base.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice horizontally and fill with your favorite deli meats, cheeses, roasted vegetables, or a simple caprese salad. The soft interior and sturdy crust make it an excellent sandwich bread.
*   **Simply On Its Own:** Often, the best way to enjoy Focaccia Genovese is warm from the oven, perhaps with just a little extra drizzle of olive oil. Its inherent flavor is satisfying enough.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Focaccia Genovese is a masterpiece, feel free to explore variations once you've mastered the basic recipe.

*   **Toppings:** Get creative with additional toppings! Olives (Kalamata, Castelvetrano), cherry tomatoes (halved), caramelized onions, thinly sliced potatoes, or minced garlic can be pressed into the dimples before the second rise.
*   **Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional for this specific focaccia, you could experiment with other fresh herbs like thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs.
*   **Flour Blends:** For a slightly different texture, you could substitute a small percentage (e.g., 50g) of the bread flour with fine semolina flour or even whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor.
*   **Spice It Up:** A pinch of red pepper flakes can add a subtle kick.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While challenging to replicate the exact texture, you can experiment with a good quality gluten-free bread flour blend. Be aware that the dough will be even stickier and may require more support during baking. The overall texture will be denser but can still be delicious.

Baking Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a rewarding experience that brings a piece of Italian culinary tradition into your home. With its irresistible aroma, golden crust, and airy crumb, it’s more than just bread – it’s a sensory delight. Follow these steps and tips, and you’ll soon be enjoying a taste of Genoa, fresh from your own oven. Buon appetito!
